tagline: Onto Mount Desert Island and once around its granite east side.
intro: Route 3 leaves Trenton, crosses by Thompson Island and a bridge onto Mount Desert Island, and comes into Bar Harbor among its old cottages. There it joins the Park Loop Road, 27 miles finished in 1958 after 37 years of work, running mostly one way and clockwise around the east side of the island by Sand Beach, Otter Cliff and Jordan Pond.

Beside it run the carriage roads that John D. Rockefeller Jr. paid for, still closed to motor cars. A side road climbs Cadillac Mountain, known as the first place in the continental U.S. to see the sunrise. That holds from October 7 to March 6.

moments.title: Thunder Hole
moments.text: Just down the shore road from Sand Beach, a crevasse in the rock where the waves come in and crash loudly.

moments.title: Jordan Pond
moments.text: A glacial tarn 150 feet deep and clear to 44 feet. Nobody swims in it, since Seal Harbor drinks it, but the Jordan Pond House serves tea and popovers on the lawn.

moments.title: Cadillac Mountain
moments.text: Green Mountain until 1918, renamed for a French adventurer who had already borrowed part of his own name from a nobleman. A cog railway ran to the top from 1883 to 1893.

practical: Acadia charges an entrance fee. Cars may use the Park Loop Road from April 15, weather permitting, until December 1. In winter only the section from the entrance station to Otter Cliff Road usually stays open to vehicles.
